title: How --shout reaches the greeting
summary: The CLI parser turns --shout (or its planned -s alias) into a boolean that selects upper-casing before the greeting is printed.

nodes.label: CLI arguments
nodes.detail: The user invokes `greet Ada --shout`. The command-line tokens reach `main(argv)`; `-s` will enter through this same path once the planned alias task is complete.

nodes.label: Shout option
nodes.detail: `ArgumentParser.add_argument` declares the `--shout` flag with `action="store_true"`. The planned alias adds `-s` to this same declaration, so both spellings share one destination.

nodes.label: Parse arguments
nodes.detail: `ap.parse_args(argv)` validates the command line and produces an argparse namespace containing the positional `name` and boolean `shout` values.

nodes.label: args.shout
nodes.detail: With `--shout` (or the planned `-s` alias), `args.shout` is `True`; without either flag it is `False`. This single boolean controls the transformation.

nodes.label: Build greeting
nodes.detail: The program first constructs the normal greeting as `Hello, {args.name}!`, preserving the existing no-flag behavior.

nodes.label: Upper-case text
nodes.detail: When `args.shout` is true, `greeting.upper()` transforms the entire greeting, including the supplied name, into `HELLO, ADA!`.

nodes.label: Printed greeting
nodes.detail: `print(greeting)` writes the selected greeting to standard output, followed by a newline. The command then returns exit code 0.
